Consult Summary:
- Adult with known asthma reports 2–3 days of increased shortness of breath on exertion, wheeze, and cough; no sputum.
- Plan: Temporarily increase inhaled steroid (Clenil) to 4 puffs twice daily, use salbutamol up to every 2–4 hours as needed, urgent face-to-face GP review; attend A&E if worsening.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Asthma with acute worsening: 2–3 days of dyspnea noted during running and now with brisk walking; associated wheeze and cough; no sputum.
- Medication use: Salbutamol (blue) used PRN and also morning/evening “to prevent;” preventer (brown/Clenil) used twice daily; precise puff count not consistently documented.
- History: No prior hospital admissions for asthma; last asthma attack 3–4 years ago; has never taken oral steroids; last asthma review ~2 years ago.
- Peak flow: Baseline reportedly ~380 (units not documented); has not checked since symptom onset.
- Atopy: Hay fever; family history of asthma (brother).
- Plan: Increase Clenil to 4 puffs twice daily while awaiting review; salbutamol up to every 2–4 hours PRN; book urgent face-to-face GP appointment in next few days for chest exam and peak flow; go to A&E if breathing worsens or requiring frequent salbutamol.

Issue 2:
- Possible eczema/atopic dermatitis: Patient reports skin issues she believes could be eczema; uses Cetraben and hydrocortisone topical; sister has eczema.
- No acute management changes discussed.

Issue 3:
- Allergic rhinitis (hay fever): Patient-reported; no specific management discussed in this consult.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler (blue): PRN; currently using multiple times daily including morning/evening; dose/route/frequency not fully documented.
- Beclomethasone dipropionate inhaler (Clenil; brown): Twice daily; number of puffs not consistently documented. Plan to increase to 4 puffs twice daily until review.
- Cetraben (topical emollient): dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hydrocortisone (topical): dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Environmental: Hay fever.
- Drug allergies: None reported.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.
- History suggestive of eczema (patient-reported; not formally confirmed).

Social History:
- Active runner; now reduced exercise tolerance.
- Smoking status, alcohol intake, and living arrangements: not documented.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed/documented (cervical screening, vaccinations, mammogram/FOBT/BMD, skin/eye checks not addressed).

Physical Examination:
- No vitals recorded.
- No physical exam performed (teleconsult).

Plan:
- Book face-to-face GP appointment within the next few days for chest examination and peak flow assessment.
- Temporarily increase Clenil to 4 puffs twice daily until review.
- Use salbutamol (blue) inhaler up to every 2–4 hours as needed for symptoms; frequent need indicates poor control and need for urgent assessment.
- Safety net: If breathing worsens or if requiring very frequent salbutamol, attend A&E/emergency department without waiting for appointment.
- At review: consider need for oral steroids and/or antibiotics depending on findings; reassess control, check inhaler technique and spacer use, update asthma action plan, and consider repeat asthma review scheduling.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements:
- Current peak flow value, vital signs, objective chest exam.
- Full medication reconciliation (exact doses/frequencies), inhaler technique/spacer use.
- Smoking status, vaccination history, and broader preventive care history.

● Internal conflicts:
- Medication list initially mentioned “Flanel/Bactroban,” later corrected to Cetraben and hydrocortisone (conflict noted; latter accepted).
- Salbutamol described as PRN but also used morning/evening as “preventative” (pattern suggests overuse; not a direct contradiction).

● Transcript quality:
- Several unclear/inaudible segments; medication names partially unclear. Recommend confirmation at in-person review.
